adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher condition is inverted: returns false when grant shortcut equals expected value, causing every test using expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken to fail
isAccessTokenId matcher reads wrong substring index: grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6) but code uses substring(3, 5), reading the last char of token type plus first char of grant

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded token prefix is 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantShortcut) as produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(). Therefore the grant shortcut occupies indices [4,6), but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which spans the last char of tokenType plus the first char of the grant shortcut, so it will read the wrong two characters for the grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deletion of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor Context(Context context) breaks compilation of any callers that construct a Context by copy

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the copy constructor `public Context(Context context)` from `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, but the diff does not show any call sites attempting to use it. Without any caller changes or compilation errors evidenced in the diff, the claim that this breaks compilation for callers cannot be verified from the provided patch alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor's rawTokenId null-check duplicates the grantType check verbatim (checks grantType twice), so null rawTokenId passes through with a misleading NPE message
matched_golden_ids: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same constructor bug: a duplicated Objects.requireNonNull check validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing rawTokenId to be null and producing an incorrect NPE message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType dereferences sessionFactory which is only assigned in postInit, causing NPE when tests or embedding code miss the pre-populated map

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, sessionFactory is only assigned in postInit(). However, getShortcutByGrantType() (and similarly getGrantTypeByShortcut()) will dereference sessionFactory when the shortcut/grant is missing from the maps ("Refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed" path). The diff shows no null-check, so if the factory is used without postInit (e.g., unit tests manually constructing it or embedding code), a missing entry will trigger a NullPointerException.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New abstract method OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() causes third-party/out-of-tree implementations to fail at deploy time with AbstractMethodError or provider-load failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (server-spi-private). Any existing/out-of-tree implementations compiled against the previous version will not have this method, making the change binary-incompatible. The new code immediately calls `gtf.getShortcut()` for every `OAuth2GrantType` factory during `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` (and elsewhere), which would trigger `AbstractMethodError` (or provider-load failure) at runtime for such third-party implementations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-credentials and other token paths not covered by OAuth2GrantTypeBase (e.g. internal-to-external exchange variants or admin-console issued tokens) construct contexts without GRANT_TYPE attribute set, silently encoding tokens as 'na' instead of the real grant shortcut

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes TokenManager.initToken() to always encode the access-token ID via TokenContextEncoderProvider using context derived from ClientSessionContext. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() reads grant type from clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE) and falls back to UNKNOWN "na" when missing. While several issuance paths in this diff do set Constants.GRANT_TYPE (e.g., OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(), refresh recreation in TokenManager.validateToken(), token exchange, password, pre-authorized code), the new design does not enforce that *all* access-token issuance paths set this attribute, so any uncovered path will silently produce an "na" grant shortcut. The finding’s specific examples (admin-console tokens, internal exchange variants, client-credentials not using the base) are not directly verifiable from the diff, but the underlying coverage risk is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher logic is inverted: returns false when substring matches expected grant shortcut, rejecting correct token IDs and accepting wrong ones
isAccessTokenId matcher indexes wrong characters: reads substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6), mixing tokenType and grant chars

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the encoded context before ':' is expected to be 6 chars (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), so the grant shortcut should be extracted with substring(4,6). The diff shows it uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which overlaps the last char of tokenType and first char of grantType, mixing fields as the finding states. This makes the matcher validate the wrong characters (and the conditional also appears inverted: it returns false when it equals expectedGrantShortcut).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing length check on items[0] before substring(3,5) causes StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of a matcher failure for short prefixes

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId.matchesSafely(), after `String[] items = item.split(":");` it only checks `items.length != 2` and then immediately calls `items[0].substring(3, 5)`. If `items[0]` is shorter than 5 characters (e.g., malformed token id prefix), this will throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException rather than returning `false` as a matcher should. The diff shows no length guard on `items[0]` before the substring call.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only exchangeClientToOIDCClient sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE; other exchange branches in StandardTokenExchangeProvider mint tokens with null grantType, encoding 'na' instead of 'te'

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient(...)` now sets `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);`. However, the claim that “other exchange branches” in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` mint tokens without setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is not verifiable from the provided diff because no other token-exchange branches/methods are shown. While the new encoder defaults to `UNKNOWN` (`"na"`) when the attribute is missing, the finding asserts missing assignments in code not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory import in StandardTokenExchangeProvider is residue of incomplete grant-type propagation

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory;` in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider`, and there is no reference to `TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory` in the shown code, so it is an unused import. However, the finding’s claim that this is a “residue of incomplete grant-type propagation” is not supported by the diff: the code explicitly propagates the grant type via `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE);`. The remaining issue is just an unused import (a style/nit), not verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor copy-paste bug: rawTokenId is never null-checked; second requireNonNull validates grantType twice, allowing null rawTokenId to produce undecodable token id instead of failing fast

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-check for `rawTokenId` is incorrect: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`, constructor). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast, and later `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will append `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, producing an invalid/ambiguous token id (e.g., ending with `:null`) rather than throwing immediately.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId has no production caller; the round-trip decode promise of the feature is unimplemented and malformed-input error semantics are unpinned

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, token IDs are encoded in production (TokenManager.initToken() uses TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) + encodeTokenId(...)), but there is no production code shown that ever calls TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(...) / DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(...); the only direct usage in the diff is the new unit test DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest. That makes the “decode later” aspect described in the new SPI/interface comment not yet integrated into any runtime path in this PR. Also, malformed-input behavior is only loosely asserted (e.g., testIncorrectGrantType catches any RuntimeException rather than pinning the exact exception/message), so error semantics aren’t strongly specified by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding getShortcut() as abstract method to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks existing third-party custom-grant implementations at deploy time (AbstractMethodError or null shortcut key)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no default implementation). Existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against the old interface will not have this method, which can cause runtime linkage failures (e.g., `AbstractMethodError`) when Keycloak calls it. The new code also immediately invokes `gtf.getShortcut()` for all grant factories during `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` and uses the returned value as a map key without null checks, so a custom implementation returning null would also break behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unit test bypasses postInit and manually seeds grant maps, leaving registration, duplicate-shortcut validation, and lazy-refresh logic with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the test calls factory.init(null) but never calls factory.postInit(...). Instead it directly assigns factory.grantsByShortcuts and factory.grantsToShortcuts (new HashMap and derived map), bypassing the real grant registration/discovery done in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() (including the duplicate-shortcut validation based on map sizes). Additionally, the lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType() / getGrantTypeByShortcut() that rely on sessionFactory are not exercised; in fact, for an unknown shortcut (e.g., "ac" in testIncorrectGrantType) getGrantTypeByShortcut() would attempt to use sessionFactory and would NPE, and the test just swallows any RuntimeException. So the finding that these mechanisms have zero meaningful coverage is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test asserting an end-to-end token request produces a token id whose prefix round-trips

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new token-id encoding/decoding logic (TokenManager#initToken now builds an AccessTokenContext and calls TokenContextEncoderProvider#encodeTokenId; DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider can parse via getTokenContextFromTokenId). The only explicit round-trip assertion added is a unit test (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest asserts decode->encode equality). The integration-side change in AssertEvents only attempts to pattern-match the event’s TOKEN_ID string, not decode it via the provider and assert it round-trips end-to-end. So the finding about missing an end-to-end/integration round-trip assertion is supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents.java has inverted logic, returning false when the substring equals the expected grant shortcut

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), matchesSafely() returns false when the parsed grant shortcut equals the expected shortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which inverts the intended condition (it should fail when NOT equal). Additionally, given the comment/encoding (6-char prefix where grant shortcut is the last 2 chars), the substring indices appear off (grant should be at positions 4-6, not 3-5), reinforcing that the matcher is incorrect per the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher uses substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6), extracting wrong characters for the grant shortcut

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the encoded context is defined in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider as 6 chars: sessionType(0-2) + tokenType(2-4) + grantType(4-6). However the matcher extracts the grant shortcut with items[0].substring(3, 5), which overlaps the last char of tokenType and the first char of grantType; it should be substring(4, 6). This will mis-validate token IDs produced by encodeTokenId().

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed Context(Context) copy constructor in OAuth2GrantType is a breaking API change unrelated to the PR intent and breaks downstream custom grant type subclasses

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the public `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (the entire constructor block is deleted). This is an API surface change that can break compilation for any downstream/custom grant implementations (or other code) that relied on cloning a Context via that constructor. The diff does not show a replacement API for copying, so the compatibility concern is real, though it’s not a runtime correctness defect within this PR itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for unknown grant types, causing 500 errors on unmapped token mint paths instead of degrading gracefully

adjudication.rationale: The diff does make `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throw `IllegalStateException` when `grantType` cannot be mapped to a shortcut (`grantShort == null`). However, the new minting flow shown in the diff does *not* produce an “unknown/unmapped token mint path” failure: when the grant type is absent from the `ClientSessionContext`, `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` explicitly degrades to `UNKNOWN` (`na`), and the factory registers `UNKNOWN` in both maps in `postInit()` so encoding succeeds. The finding’s claim about 500s on “unmapped token mint paths” is not verifiable from the diff and conflicts with the explicit null->UNKNOWN handling added here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId decoder SPI has zero callers in this diff, making half the framework dead code including hot-reload concurrency logic

adjudication.rationale: The claim that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` has zero callers in this diff is false: it is directly invoked multiple times in the newly added `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` (e.g., `provider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(tokenId)` in several tests). Additionally, the encoder/decoder framework is actively wired into runtime token creation (`TokenManager.initToken()` now calls `encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` and `encoder.encodeTokenId(...)`), so it is not “half dead code” based on what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.GRANT_TYPE aliases OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE, creating a duplicate public name for the same constant

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `public static final String GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE;` in `org.keycloak.models.Constants`, but this does not create a duplicate public name in any Java sense: `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` and `OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` are different fully-qualified symbols (namespaced by class). The change is simply an alias/value reuse for a key string and is used throughout the diff as `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` for `ClientSessionContext` attributes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UNKNOWN sentinel uses 'na' while other unknown markers in the same file use 'un', creating inconsistent sentinels in the context encoding

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show different “unknown” shortcuts: SessionType.UNKNOWN and TokenType.UNKNOWN use "un" in AccessTokenContext, while grantType’s UNKNOWN sentinel is the constant DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN = "na". However, this is not a verifiable defect: grantType is not an enum here, and the factory explicitly maps "na" <-> "na" in postInit, so behavior remains consistent within the implementation. This reads as a minor consistency/style preference rather than a bug or important non-bug issue grounded in broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor checks grantType twice instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to pass validation and produce corrupted token ids

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null-checks include `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` (i.e., `grantType` is checked twice). This means `rawTokenId` is never validated for null and could be stored as null, potentially leading to malformed/"corrupted" encoded token IDs when `encodeTokenId` appends `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic: returns false when the grant shortcut matches the expected value

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the parsed grant shortcut equals the expected value: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` which inverts the intended logic (it should fail when it does NOT equal). This makes the matcher reject correct token IDs. (Additionally, the substring indices appear off for a 6-char prefix, but the finding’s inverted-logic claim is directly verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId uses substring(3,5) instead of the correct substring(4,6) for the grant shortcut offset

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the token-id encoding introduced elsewhere in the diff is 6 chars before ':' (2 sessionType + 2 tokenType + 2 grantType), so the grant shortcut is at indices [4,6) (0-based). The matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which selects the 4th–5th characters instead of the 5th–6th, so it checks the wrong slice and can mis-validate token IDs like "trltcc:..." where the grant shortcut is "cc" at positions 4–5.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext.java constructor null-checks grantType twice (copy-paste) so rawTokenId is never null-checked

adjudication.rationale: In the new file `AccessTokenContext.java`, the constructor does `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId`. This copy/paste mistake means `rawTokenId` is never null-validated and can be stored as null despite the intent, potentially causing later NPEs or invalid encoded token IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OAuth2GrantType.java removes the public Context(Context) copy constructor, breaking third-party grant-type extensions without a deprecation cycle

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly deletes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (the entire constructor block is removed). Any external code (including third-party grant implementations) that previously used this constructor will fail to compile unless updated. This is an API/SPI compatibility concern visible in the diff, though it’s not a runtime correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException in TokenManager.initToken, turning an unknown grant type into a total token-issuance failure instead of using the 'na' fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes TokenManager.initToken() unconditionally encode the access token ID via TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...). In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(), an unmapped grantType causes an IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType()) returns null. While getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext() falls back to "na" only when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is null, it does not guard against a non-null but unrecognized grantType value (e.g., from extensions or other token-issuance paths), so token issuance could fail hard in that edge case. However, the diff also updates built-in grant factories to provide shortcuts and sets GRANT_TYPE in several flows, so this is not clearly a guaranteed defect for core behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TokenManager.java silently changes the jti format from a bare UUID to '<6-char-prefix>:<uuid>', breaking existing consumers that assume UUID-ness

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the access token `jti` format in `TokenManager.initToken(...)` from `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (a UUID) to `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`, where `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` returns a 6-character context prefix plus `':'` plus the raw UUID (e.g., `onrtcc:<uuid>`). This is a deliberate behavior change (tests were updated to expect the new format in `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)`), not an internally verifiable correctness defect. However, it is a real backward-compatibility/API-contract concern because existing external consumers that assume `jti` is a bare UUID could break, and nothing in the diff indicates a compatibility flag, versioning, or deprecation path—so the review finding is valid as a non-bug impact/risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId decode half has zero production call sites, emitting a permanent wire format ahead of its consumer

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, production code starts *encoding* access token IDs with a new structured format (`TokenManager.initToken`: `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)`), but there is no production usage shown for the corresponding *decode* path (`TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` / `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId`). The only visible call sites for decoding are in the new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest`. That makes the finding about “decode half has zero production call sites” diff-grounded, and it also highlights an architecture concern: the PR commits to a new token-id wire format before any runtime consumer is demonstrated in this change set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Null-check for rawTokenId was dropped in AccessTokenContext constructor: grantType is checked twice and rawTokenId never checked, allowing null rawTokenId producing token IDs ending in ':null'

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` mistakenly checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` can be `null` without error, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield token IDs ending with `:null`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher in AssertEvents reads wrong indices (3-4 instead of 4-5) for the grant shortcut and the comparison is inverted so a match returns false
matched_golden_ids: In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same two problems as the golden comment: the grant shortcut substring indices are off (it should use indices 4–5 via substring(4,6), not 3–4) and the equality/comparison logic is inverted such that a matching grant shortcut incorrectly returns false instead of true (when combined with the UUID check).

adjudication_records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher never positively verifies the grant type, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken tests assert nothing about grant-type encoding

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut check is inverted and the substring range is off. It does `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which rejects IDs that *do* contain the expected shortcut, and then returns true as long as the raw part is a UUID. Also, per the new encoding (`sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grantType(2)`), the grant shortcut is at positions 4-6 (0-based substring(4,6)), not substring(3,5). As written, the matcher does not positively verify the expected grant-type encoding for expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/etc., and likely fails when the shortcut is correct.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public copy constructor Context(Context context) in OAuth2GrantType.Context was deleted without deprecation or replacement, breaking compilation of existing extensions

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.OAuth2GrantType.Context` (see the deleted block in `OAuth2GrantType.java`). Since this was a public API surface and no alternative copy/clone method or deprecation shim is added in the diff, any existing code (including extensions) that instantiated `new Context(existingContext)` will fail to compile after this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: String getShortcut() added to public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI interface without a default implementation, breaking all third-party implementations and making the scheme mandatory

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface (`server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java`) without providing a `default` implementation. In Java, adding a non-default method to an interface is a source/binary incompatible change for all existing implementers; the PR updates Keycloak’s built-in grant factories to implement it, but any external/third-party implementations would fail to compile/load without changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Decoder in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hard-requires encoded context length of 6 while interface javadoc says shortcuts are 'usually like 3-letters', so documented implementations throw IllegalArgumentException on decode

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(), decoding hard-requires encodedContext.length() == 6 and explicitly parses 2 chars each for sessionType, tokenType, and grantType (substring(4,6)). However OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut() javadoc says shortcuts are “usually like 3-letters”, and encodeTokenId() will blindly concatenate whatever shortcut the grant factory returns. If a grant implementation returns a 3-letter shortcut, encodeTokenId() will generate a context prefix longer than 6, and decoding will throw IllegalArgumentException, meaning tokens produced by such a grant cannot be decoded by the same provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token context encoding framework wired unconditionally into initToken for every access token, changing jti/Details.TOKEN_ID format realm-wide without a feature flag or rollout gate

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows TokenManager.initToken now always obtains TokenContextEncoderProvider and encodes the token ID (`token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx));`), which changes the access token `jti`/Details.TOKEN_ID format from a raw generated ID to a prefixed `xxxxxx:<rawId>` form across all access tokens. There is no feature flag/conditional visible around this wiring. This is a real, diff-grounded compatibility/rollout concern rather than a provable functional defect within the diff itself (tests were updated to accept the new format).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Constants.GRANT_TYPE is a bare alias of the generic OAuth2 grant_type string, so clientSessionContext attributes set under the raw OAuth2 name are silently reinterpreted as the encoding framework's grant-type note, potentially blocking token issuance

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Constants.GRANT_TYPE = OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (i.e., the literal OAuth2 parameter name `"grant_type"`) and uses it as a `ClientSessionContext` attribute key (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` in several grant flows and in refresh). The new token-id encoding reads this same attribute (`DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`) and will fail issuance if the value is not mappable to a registered grant shortcut (`encodeTokenId` throws `IllegalStateException` when `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(...)` returns null). This creates a concrete namespace/collision risk because the key is not namespaced and could be used elsewhere for other purposes; however, the diff does not show an actual conflicting writer, so the “blocking issuance” scenario is not directly verifiable from this PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor at line 62 has broken null validation: requireNonNull checks grantType a second time instead of rawTokenId, so null rawTokenId slips through and produces a malformed jti ending in ':null' that round-trips as the literal string 'null', silently mis-keying revocation lookups and downstream colon-splitting consumers

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null check is incorrect: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of validating `rawTokenId` (so `rawTokenId` can be null). This is directly visible in `AccessTokenContext.java`. If a null `rawTokenId` is passed, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will concatenate `":" + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing a token id suffix of `:null`, and `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` would then parse the raw id as the literal string `"null"`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit duplicate shortcut check only compares grant shortcuts against each other, so a grant shortcut colliding with a SessionType, TokenType, or 'na' shortcut passes validation but corrupts token-context decoding for every token

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider, token-id decoding is position-based: first 2 chars are SessionType, next 2 are TokenType, last 2 are grant shortcut (substring(0,2), (2,4), (4,6)). Therefore a grant shortcut colliding with a SessionType/TokenType shortcut does not affect decoding because they live in different fixed positions and are looked up in separate maps. The factory’s postInit size check is aimed at detecting duplicate grant IDs/shortcuts among grants; collisions with session/token shortcuts would not “corrupt decoding for every token” per the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher at line 479 has inverted logic (returns failure when the grant shortcut matches) and wrong offset (substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6)), causing assertions to fail on correctly-encoded token IDs and pass on wrong-grant IDs, neutralizing regression detection for the token-id encoding

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), the matcher logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` makes it fail when the expected shortcut matches and succeed when it doesn’t (as long as the raw id is a UUID). Additionally, the offset is wrong: token IDs are encoded as 2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grant shortcut (see DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId), so the grant shortcut should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `(3, 5)`. This would cause assertions to fail on correctly-encoded IDs and pass on incorrect-grant IDs, weakening regression detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId at line 64 throws IllegalArgumentException with the attacker-influenced token id embedded in the message, creating a 500-class exception path and log-injection vector for untrusted jti inputs instead of a graceful UNKNOWN result

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, malformed encodedTokenId values that contain ':' but have an unexpected context length or unknown shortcuts cause IllegalArgumentException with the full encodedTokenId embedded in the message (e.g., "Incorrect token id: '" + encodedTokenId + "'..."). The diff does not show how/where this exception is handled, so the claim that it necessarily creates a 500-class path and log-injection is not verifiable from the diff alone. However, the finding is grounded in the new parsing behavior: it is not consistently "graceful UNKNOWN" for attacker-controlled token ids and it does reflect untrusted input in exception text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.java isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted boolean logic: returns false when grant shortcut equals expected, causing expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken to verify the opposite of intended behavior

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(), matchesSafely() returns false when the extracted grant shortcut equals expectedGrantShortcut: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, which inverts the intended logic (it should fail when not equal). Additionally, given the comment/encoding (2 chars sessionType + 2 chars tokenType + 2 chars grantType), the grant shortcut should start at index 4 (substring(4,6)), not substring(3,5). This causes the new expectations in expectCodeToToken/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectAuthReqIdToToken to validate the opposite (or wrong slice) of the intended grant type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents matcher only validates grant shortcut (chars 3-4) and raw-ID UUID, not sessionType or tokenType slots, leaving 2/3 of the encoded context unasserted

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(String), the matcher splits on ':' and then only inspects a 2-char slice intended to correspond to the grant shortcut plus checks that the raw part is a UUID. It does not assert anything about the other encoded context fields (sessionType and tokenType) that occupy the first 4 characters of the 6-char encoded context produced by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(). Therefore, most of the new token-id context is not being verified by these event assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext.java constructor checks grantType for null a second time instead of rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId to flow into encodeTokenId producing 'null' token IDs

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` mistakenly checks `grantType` a second time instead of `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without being rejected. Later, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, which would yield a token id ending with the literal string `"null"` if `rawTokenId` is null (string concatenation with null), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testIncorrectGrantType uses catch-all catch (RuntimeException) with empty body, never asserting the specific exception type or message
matched_golden_ids: Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the test catches a generic RuntimeException rather than the specific expected exception (IllegalArgumentException), making the test imprecise. The candidate also notes the empty catch body and missing assertions, which aligns with the golden concern about precision in exception testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Round-trip-only test coverage re-encodes decoded values and compares to input, validating only encode∘decode = identity with no independent literal-output assertion for the token ID wire format

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest, encodeTokenId() is only exercised by re-encoding an AccessTokenContext that was first produced by getTokenContextFromTokenId() (e.g., testSuccessClientCredentialsToken/testSuccessOfflineToken). While the tests do independently assert decoded fields against expected literals, there is no test that constructs an AccessTokenContext directly and asserts the exact encoded wire-format string output. This means encoder and decoder could share a consistent but wrong encoding scheme and still pass the encode step checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No end-to-end test asserting the grant attribute lands in the encoded token ID in TokenManager.initToken/refresh paths; event matcher coverage is bugged and setAttribute placement regressions would go undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an end-to-end assertion via AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...), but that matcher is incorrect and effectively does not validate the grant shortcut. In testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/.../AssertEvents.java, matchesSafely uses items[0].substring(3, 5) (should be the grant segment at indexes 4..6 given 2+2+2 layout) and it returns false when the extracted shortcut equals expectedGrantShortcut (logic inverted). As a result, for normal 6-char contexts like "trltcc", substring(3,5) yields "tc" (tokenType last char + grant first char), almost never equals the expected grant, so the matcher degenerates to only checking the raw UUID and would let wrong-grant encodings pass undetected—matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test hand-rebuilds factory's shortcut maps instead of exercising postInit's duplicate-shortcut validation, and passes null session so getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext (the production-wired method) is never tested

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before(), the test constructs DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, calls init(null), then manually populates factory.grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts (and never calls postInit), so the postInit() logic that builds maps from OAuth2GrantType factories and performs the duplicate-shortcut validation (size check) is not exercised. The test also instantiates DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider with a null KeycloakSession and only tests getTokenContextFromTokenId()/encodeTokenId(); it never calls the production-wired path getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(), which in production uses session (e.g., AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)) and clientSessionContext attributes. This is a concrete test coverage/design issue grounded in the diff, not a functional defect in the implementation itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New SPI interface method getShortcut() added to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory without a default implementation, causing AbstractMethodError for third-party grant factories at startup (server fails to boot after upgrade)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut();` to the public SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (no `default` implementation). In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, the code iterates all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on each. Any third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` compiled against the old interface (without `getShortcut`) would not have that method, and invoking it will throw `AbstractMethodError`, plausibly during server startup when `postInit` runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IllegalStateException with no fallback in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId when a grant-type attribute has no registered shortcut, causing token endpoint 500s for unregistered grant types

adjudication.rationale: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` does throw `IllegalStateException` if `factory.getShortcutByGrantType(tokenContext.getGrantType())` returns null, but the diff also shows the factory pre-populates `grantsToShortcuts/grantsByShortcuts` for *all* registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations in `postInit()`, plus a built-in fallback mapping for `UNKNOWN` (`"na"`). Additionally, `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` falls back to `UNKNOWN` when the grant type attribute is missing. An actually “unregistered grant type” would not be processed to the point of token creation (no grant provider), so the claim that this causes token endpoint 500s for unregistered grant types is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy token IDs containing ':' are silently misparsed in getTokenContextFromTokenId: pre-colon segment treated as encoded context, and a 6-char prefix validated as a known shortcut can throw IllegalArgumentException

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId, any token id containing ':' is treated as the new format: it splits on the first ':' and then requires the pre-colon segment to be exactly 6 chars and match known shortcuts, otherwise it throws IllegalArgumentException. This means an unencoded/legacy token id that happens to contain ':' (and especially one with a 6-char prefix) could be misinterpreted as an encoded context or cause an exception. The diff does not show that legacy Keycloak token IDs ever included ':', so this is a robustness/compatibility edge-case concern rather than a verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted comparison logic and wrong substring offsets (3,5 instead of 4,6), so it never correctly verifies the grant shortcut and can reject correctly-encoded tokens

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the matcher returns false when the extracted shortcut equals the expected one (`if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), which inverts the intended logic. Additionally, based on the token id encoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider (`sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2)+':'+rawId`), the grant shortcut should be at indices 4..6, but the matcher uses `substring(3,5)`, which overlaps tokenType and grantType. This will reject correctly encoded token IDs and fail to properly verify the grant shortcut.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate null-check of grantType in AccessTokenContext constructor (with wrong message on second check) means rawTokenId is never validated and null rawTokenId is accepted silently

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` is a duplicated null-check of `grantType` and never validates `rawTokenId` (diff: `AccessTokenContext.java` lines in constructor). As a result, `rawTokenId` can be null without throwing, contrary to intent and the error message, and later `encodeTokenId` will concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` producing an invalid/"null" token id rather than failing fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Access-token jti format change from bare UUID to prefixed IDs is a breaking contract change for external consumers (DB columns, event pipelines, caches) with no opt-out, migration note, or rollout flag

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes how the access token ID/jti is generated: TokenManager.initToken() no longer uses a bare generated UUID (`token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())`) and instead encodes a prefixed value via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` (yielding strings like `trltcc:1234` as shown in the new tests). This is a behavior/format contract change for `Details.TOKEN_ID` and token `jti` consumers. The diff shows no configuration/feature flag/opt-out path; the SPI is registered as internal and the default factory is always available via service registration, and tests are updated to expect the new format. While not a provable 'defect' from the diff alone, it is a concrete backward-compatibility/rollout concern created by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postInit calls new abstract method getShortcut() on OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default implementation, causing AbstractMethodError and startup failure for third-party grant providers compiled against the previous interface

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no default implementation. In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, the code iterates over all `OAuth2GrantType` provider factories, casts them to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any third-party grant provider factory compiled against the previous version of the interface (without `getShortcut()`) would not implement this method, and the runtime call would result in an `AbstractMethodError`, potentially failing startup during `postInit`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws raw IllegalArgumentException (HTTP 500) for malformed attacker-supplied token IDs instead of an OAuth 4xx invalid_request/invalid_grant error

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() can throw IllegalArgumentException for malformed/unknown encoded token IDs (e.g., wrong context length or unknown shortcuts). However, the diff does not show any call path where this method is invoked on attacker-supplied inputs in an HTTP request flow, nor that such an exception would surface as an HTTP 500 instead of being translated to an OAuth 4xx error. The only newly shown usage is encoding token IDs in TokenManager.initToken(), not decoding/parsing incoming tokens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: IllegalArgumentException message embeds the raw attacker-controlled token id

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new IllegalArgumentException throws in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() that embed the full input `encodedTokenId` in the exception message (e.g., "Incorrect token id: '" + encodedTokenId + "'...", and similar). Since `encodedTokenId` comes from a method parameter and can be attacker-controlled in callers that parse incoming tokens, this can lead to log-forging/noise or sensitive string reflection if the exception is logged/propagated. However, the diff alone does not show that this exception message is returned to clients or logged unsafely, so it’s a grounded concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AccessTokenContext constructor copy-pastes the grantType null check instead of checking rawTokenId, so null rawTokenId passes with a misleading error message

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the null check for `rawTokenId` is incorrect: it calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This both (a) allows `rawTokenId` to be null without being rejected and (b) would throw a misleading exception message tied to the wrong parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Token-issuing paths that never set Constants.GRANT_TYPE silently encode the placeholder "na" into the token id with no log or warning, making the round-trip lossy and masking wiring bugs

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that if `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` is not present on the `ClientSessionContext`, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` falls back to `UNKNOWN` (`"na"`) with no logging/warning (`if (grantType == null) { grantType = UNKNOWN; }`). Since `encodeTokenId` will then encode that shortcut (factory explicitly maps `UNKNOWN` in `postInit`), missing wiring will silently produce token IDs containing `...na:` rather than failing fast or surfacing an issue. However, the diff does not prove there exists a specific token-issuing path that fails to set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`; many paths in the diff do set it (e.g., `OAuth2GrantTypeBase#createTokenResponse`, refresh token path, token exchange, etc.), so the claim about “paths that never set” is not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getShortcutByGrantType returns null for unregistered grant types, causing IllegalStateException and a raw 500 during token issuance in encodeTokenId

adjudication.rationale: In the new encoding path, `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` throws if `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType()` returns null ("Cannot encode token with unknown grantType..."). `getShortcutByGrantType()` does indeed return null when the grant type isn’t known in `grantsToShortcuts` and `sessionFactory.getProviderFactory(OAuth2GrantType.class, grantType)` also returns null (i.e., truly unregistered/unknown). This would surface as an unhandled `IllegalStateException` during `TokenManager.initToken()` (token issuance). However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that such an unknown grant type can occur in normal request routing (grant selection is typically based on `grant_type`, and the built-in grants now all provide shortcuts), so it’s more of a robustness/edge-case concern than a clearly demonstrated defect.
